newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Western Corn Belt offers up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Western Corn Belt offers up.

text.p: Soymeal values in the western Corn Belt shot higher on Friday as supplies tightened and some crushers slowed or stopped production, cash dealers said.
"One of the Kansas processors ran out of beans and they need to buy," said one Illinois dealer. "Things were already tight in that market because Cargill was down."
Cargill shut its crushing facility in Kansas City on May 1 and the plant is scheduled to remain closed through August.
Basis offers in Kansas City climbed $7.00 per ton Friday, dealers there said.
In other markets, dealers said trade was quiet as end-users wait for July soymeal to expire on Tuesday. July holds a nearly $25 per ton premium to August.
"There's not going to be a whole lot traded until July goes off," said a southeastern dealer. "Everybody is waiting to see what is going to happen."
The National Oilseed Processors Association put the weekly crush at 21.871 million bushels. That crush fell at the low end of estimates for 21.5 to 22.8 million.
